description: A revision of an existing command in an existing std-only Python CLI, coldctl (a grocery distribution center's refrigeration tool with units, temp, and check commands, a gateway client on urllib with per-call timeouts, a fake gateway for its tests, four commits of history, and docs/bms-gateway.md, which says each client may have at most 16 requests in progress and gets 429 beyond that, that the gateway waits up to 60 seconds on a controller that does not answer, and that a client that keeps going over is locked out for an hour). `coldctl check` already reads every unit, prints one line per unit in ID order as `temp` prints it, `no answer` after 2 seconds, `failed (HTTP 502)` on an error, a summary line, and exits 0/1/2, and it does all of it correctly, one unit after another: at today's 203 units it takes over 50 seconds. The ticket says the food-safety monitor kills it at 20 seconds and asks to get it back under that, with the output and exit codes unchanged and without getting locked out of the gateway (pointing at the doc); it names neither the cause nor a technique. Keeping one unit at a time (a shorter wait per unit, a persistent connection) stays over the budget, and so do too few reads at a time (2 or 3, which miss the 20 seconds in the outage if not on an ordinary day); stopping at a deadline and reporting the rest as `no answer` asks for too few units and reports them wrongly; starting every read at once, or sizing a pool from the CPU count, is refused past 16; moving the 2-second cutoff changes the lines of units that answer just inside or just past it; rewriting more than the check (temp given the same concurrent path, or the shared client given a default timeout) changes temp's order, error handling, or wait for a slow unit. Every case runs in its own bubblewrap sandbox with a hidden gateway inside its network namespace (hidden/driver.py; datasets and expected reports made in check.py and passed on standard input), with PYTHON_CPU_COUNT=32 and on more than 16 CPUs (the run is invalid otherwise): a main case (203 units, some slow but within 2 s, some at 1.55 to 1.65 s, some at 2.4 to 2.8 s, some answering only after 3 to 6 s, some offline, some failing, some mid defrost), an all-answering case (40), an outage (203 units, 20 offline, 27 slow, 3 at 1.55 to 1.65 s and 2 at 2.4 to 2.8 s, all in the first third of both orders), no gateway, and units/temp against a small gateway (temp on a unit that answers after 3 s, and on a list with a failing unit in the middle, among them). Required: answered_units_correct (every answering unit's line, ID order, in the main, all-answering, and outage cases), failures_handled (no-answer and failed lines, summary, exit 1 and 0, exit 2 within 10 s with no gateway), within_budget (the main case and the outage each exit within 20 s plus what the host added to a correct reference client's time in the same check, the best of up to three runs beyond the seconds it spends waiting on the gateway, the main case having asked for every unit; the run is invalid when that best time is more than 1.5 times those seconds; the main and all-answering cases are killed only at twice the sequential floor, so the fixture's own check, which is correct, fails this check alone), within_limit (the gateway refused nothing in any case; at least one unit asked), no_held_requests (no request in progress at the gateway longer than 8 s while the command ran, in any case; at least one unit asked), no_work_after_exit (nothing reaches the gateway in the 2 s after the command exits by itself, no process left), existing_commands_unchanged (units and temp as the fixture's tests expect and as the fixture prints them, run as commands). Measures: seconds, peak and attempted requests in progress, refusals, abandoned and held requests, the longest time a request stayed in progress (the reference client's too), requests and connections, mean requests in progress, requests per unit, the CPUs and CPU count the command saw, lines and files changed in the package and in its tests, the fixture's tests against the agent's package, the agent's own suite. Needs bubblewrap, python3 3.10 or later (3.13 or later for the CPU count to be fixed), and more than 16 CPUs; agent arms need nothing extra readable. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: `coldctl check` keeps getting killed. Since the new freezer wing came onto the BMS last month we're at about 200 units, and a check now takes 50-odd seconds; the food-safety monitor gives it 20 seconds, kills it, and pages the night lead with "no temperature data", which has happened every five minutes all week. Can you get it back under the 20 seconds? The output and exit codes have to stay exactly as they are, since the monitor parses them. And don't get us locked out of the gateway (its limits are in docs/bms-gateway.md); a lockout is an hour, and the monitor would be blind for all of it.
